back: Will (present) and Would (past) describe characteristic behavior or habits [8].
Used for things that are/were always true (e.g., 'Cold weather will kill certain plants') [8].
Do NOT use 'will' or 'would' for habits on a specific single past occasion [8].
Stressing 'will' or 'would' can show disapproval (e.g., 'She just won't do the washing') [8].
Used to draw conclusions about current states (e.g., 'Martina will be at home by now') [8].
Both work for repeated past events, but 'would' needs a clear time reference [8].
Use 'used to' (not 'would') for past states that changed (e.g., 'The factory used to be there') [8].
Do NOT use 'used to' or 'would'; use past simple [8].
To talk about an unreal past situation (imaginary or unfulfilled) [8].
To say a past situation actually happened (e.g., 'few people will have seen last night's eclipse') [8].
